title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X_• is a simplicial object and C** = C**(X_•, k) is a bigraded differential k-algebra with divided powers. It is (anti)commutative and alternating. It contains an element T in C^{1,0}, and T̄ = dT lies in C^{0,1}. Since T̄ has odd total degree in an alternating algebra, T̄∧T̄ = 0.

Two properties are recorded:
- (B) For p > 0 the Koszul-type sequence 0 → C^{p,0} → C^{p,1} → C^{p,2} → … (each map is T̄∧) is exact.
- For p = 0 its cohomology is 0 in degrees ≤ 1 and H^{n-1}(X_•, k) in degree n ≥ 2. This comes from the PD-Poincaré-lemma-type resolution 0 → k → Λ^0Φ → Λ^1Φ → ….

On this page.
- Grothendieck defines DR^{p,q} = Ker(T̄∧ : C^{p,q+1} → C^{p,q+2}). The machine transcription's 'F_·' is T̄· (multiplication by T̄).
- He gets two maps:
  - u = T̄∧ : C^{p,q} → DR^{p,q}, which is surjective for p ≠ 0 by exactness;
  - the inclusion i : DR^{p,q} ↪ C^{p,q+1}, of bidegree (0,1).
- These satisfy Im i = Ker u and i∘u = T̄∧ (margin). There is also (C): i(x)·i(y) = 0. When p > 0, elements of i(DR) are multiples of T̄, so the product contains T̄² = 0.
- The margin notes that (C) can fail on i(DR^{0,*})·i(DR^{0,*}), since there Ker T̄ is strictly bigger than Im T̄.

Goal. Put on DR** a structure of commutative (alternating) bigraded differential algebra with divided powers. It should satisfy:
- u is a morphism of such structures: u(xy) = u(x)u(y);
- module-type compatibilities i(x·u(y)) = i(x)y and i(u(y)·x) = y·i(x);
- i has bidegree (0,1) and anticommutes with the differential.

Grothendieck observes that these requirements almost determine the structure. The only exceptions are the products xy and divided powers x^{(i)} (i ≥ 2) of elements of DR^{0,*} not in Im u.

Argument sketched.
- On Im u × Im u the product is forced by u(x)u(y) = u(xy). Apply i, so that i(ux·uy) = T̄(xy) = (T̄x)y.
- It remains to show existence and uniqueness of Im u × DR → DR and DR × Im u → DR satisfying relations 2 and 3. Define x·u(y) := i^{-1}(i(x)y).
  - (a) i(x)y lies in Ker T̄, because T̄·i(x)y = (T̄ i(x))y = 0, as x ∈ DR.
  - (b) It depends only on u(y). If u(y) = 0, then T̄y = 0, so y lies in i(DR). Hence i(x)y = 0 by (C).
- Relation 3 is handled the same way.
- The next page shows that divided powers descend along u. This uses (D): DR is stable under divided powers, since y^{(i)} = (T̄z)^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)} = 0 for i ≥ 2.
- It then isolates the residual data (E): products DR^{0,p} × DR^{0,q} → DR^{0,p+q} and divided powers γ^i on DR^{0,*}, which must be specified separately.

In modern terms. For p > 0, DR is identified with the quotient C/Ker(T̄) = C/T̄C, which is an algebra since T̄C is an ideal. It is also identified with the ideal T̄C, embedded with a degree shift. The page transports the PD-algebra structure through this identification and locates exactly where the transport fails: the p = 0 column, where H(C, T̄∧) ≠ 0. It serves the larger aim of recovering the divided-power de Rham complex from simplicial cochain data.
errors: The page initially asserts i(DR)·i(u DR) = 0, and then generalises to i(DR^{p,q})·i(DR^{p',q'}) = 0. This holds only when one factor has p > 0, i.e. lies in Im T̄. The margin correctly notes the failure for i(DR^{0,*})·i(DR^{0,*}). The text treats (C) somewhat loosely before that correction.
The display 'u: C** → D**' is a slip for DR**.
In step (b), 'i.e. y ∈ DR' is shorthand for y ∈ i(DR) = Ker T̄ = Im T̄, which is valid only for p > 0. The degree hypotheses needed are left implicit.
No sign conventions for the anticommutation of i with d and with products are fixed. This is minor, since the structure is only claimed up to the stated ambiguities.

ideas.what: Identify DR := Ker(T̄∧) with the quotient C/Ker(T̄∧) via u = T̄∧ and transport the multiplicative PD-structure. Exactness of the T̄-Koszul sequence for p > 0 gives surjectivity of u.
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of a CDGA (PD-algebra) by the ideal generated/annihilated by an odd element squaring to zero; Koszul/Bockstein-type cohomology of multiplication by an odd degree-1 element
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homological algebra; PD-algebra quotients by PD-ideals in Berthelot's crystalline theory (1974)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; the 1976 IHES lecture on the PD de Rham complex was not published by Grothendieck

ideas.what: Module-type compatibilities i(x u(y)) = i(x)y and i(u(y)x) = y i(x), together with i(x)i(y) = 0, characterising the product on DR almost uniquely.
ideas.modern_name: DR as a square-zero shifted ideal T̄C ⊂ C; a 'connecting map' i of degree +1 that is a derivation-like module map

ideas.what: Isolating the obstruction to transporting the structure: products and divided powers on the p = 0 column, where H(C^{0,*}, T̄∧) ≅ H^{*-1}(X_•, k) ≠ 0. Hence extra 'canonical' data (E) is needed.
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to strictifying a multiplicative structure at cochain level (Steenrod-type / E∞ issues on cochains)

ideas.what: Stability of Ker T̄ under divided powers in C, since (T̄z)^{(i)} = T̄^i z^{(i)} = 0 for i ≥ 2 (next page, used to descend PD operations along u).
ideas.modern_name: PD-ideal generated by an element of odd degree / divided powers vanishing on T̄C

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies precisely that, outside the p = 0 column, the PD-CDGA structure on the 'de Rham' piece DR** is forced by cochain data. The only free input is the products and divided powers on DR^{0,*}, which see H^*(X_•, k). He leaves the required 'axiomes divers' for this extra data unspecified (next page). It is an unfinished attempt to characterise the PD de Rham complex axiomatically via simplicial cochains with a distinguished element T. In spirit it is close to later 'cochain models' of de Rham/crystalline cohomology, but technically elementary.
missed.quote: Cette structure sur DR** est presque déterminée par ces propriétés ... à C déterminé près des produits xy et des puissances divisées x^{(i)} (i≥2) quand x,y de degré complémentaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mildly relevant to the history of cochain-level models of PD/derived de Rham cohomology (Illusie, Bhatt, décalage-type constructions). The page itself contains only routine homological algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical working page transporting a multiplicative divided-power structure along the identification Ker(T̄∧) ≅ C/Ker(T̄∧). The arguments are standard. The only point of interest is the precise isolation of the residual data on the p = 0 column, as part of an unpublished program on the PD de Rham complex.
transcription_corrections: 'F_·' throughout is T̄· / T̄∧ (multiplication by T̄ = dT), not F.
'u: C** → D**' should be 'u: C** → DR**'.
Margin: 'i∘u = T̄∧(·)' (written T̄∧( )), and 'Im i = Ker u'.
Slanted margin probably reads 'donc (C) inexact pour i(DR^{0p})·i(DR^{0q}) ≠ 0', i.e. (C) fails on the p = 0 column.
Under the arrow: 'épi si p ≠ 0', and the vertical inclusion DR^{p,q} ⊂ C^{p,q+1}.
